title: Adaptive system identification vs fixed and periodically recalibrated models under cold-plate drift
research_question: Does adaptive identification of the cold-plate resistance reduce prediction error and unsafe decisions compared with a fixed-parameter twin and with periodic recalibration, and can drift be detected early from prediction residuals?
hypothesis: Conditions: plant-only cold-plate resistance drift none / slow ramp (+0.005 K/W per h from 1 h) / fast ramp (+0.015 K/W per h from 1 h) / step (+0.02 K/W at 1.5 h) x ambient 25 and 35 C; S6 load profile, 4 h, clean plates at start, instant plant, measured clock sensitivity and leakage slope (E011 base); 5 seeds. Policies: joint_fixed (joint_fb with diagnostics), joint_recal (refit every 30 min), joint_adaptive (RLS, forgetting 0.95), joint_robust (E008 bias correction; different overload fallback, so its energy is not compared). H1 (no harm without drift): in both no-drift conditions joint_recal and joint_adaptive are within +/-0.5% of joint_fixed in energy per successful task (95% CI) and record no more chip-seconds above 80 C. H2 (drift makes a fixed model unsafe): joint_fixed exceeds 80 C (seed mean > 0) in at least 4 of the 6 drift conditions. H3 (adaptation restores safety): wherever joint_fixed exceeds 80 C, joint_adaptive's chip-seconds above 80 C are at least 80% lower. H4 (adaptive beats periodic after a step): in both step conditions joint_adaptive records fewer chip-seconds above 80 C than joint_recal (seed means). H5 (prediction error): joint_adaptive's mean absolute error in predicting the peak junction temperature is at most half of joint_fixed's in every drift condition. H6 (cost): where joint_fixed records no time above 80 C, joint_adaptive's energy per successful task is at most 2% above joint_fixed's (95% CI upper bound). H7 (detection): a Page-Hinkley test (delta 0.5 K, lambda 10 K) on joint_fixed's residuals alarms within 30 min of the step in every seed of both step conditions and in no seed of the no-drift conditions.
null_hypothesis: Adaptive identification changes neither prediction error nor safety relative to a fixed model.
controlled_variables: drift exists only in the simulated plant, never in the models
evaluation_criteria: Thermal outcomes and diagnostics as seed means; energy as paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; alarm times per seed.
randomization: Workloads drawn per seed and shared across policies.
measurement_boundary: Simulated facility boundary of one 8-accelerator node; nothing measured.
known_limitations: The drift is a uniform resistance increase on all chips; real fouling is uneven. The estimator sees the mean junction temperature and mean chip heat only. Detection thresholds are fixed design choices. The adaptive model may only become more conservative (Delta_R clipped at 0). Simulation only.
disclosure: Known before registration: E005/E008 (twin mismatch, joint_robust) and unit tests of the estimators on synthetic data, including one 1 h run of joint_adaptive with a +0.02 K/W step at 15 min (test: final Delta_R near 0.02). E015 was running; its results had not been looked at. No E016 cell was run before registration.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
